tools.docx-to-png.faqs.0.answer: The tool renders the document in your browser following Word's layout, splits it into pages, and saves each page as a PNG image with the layout close to the original.
tools.docx-to-png.faqs.1.question: Which Word formats are supported?

tools.docx-to-png.faqs.2.question: What's the difference between PNG and JPG?

tools.docx-to-png.faqs.3.question: Is the document uploaded to a server?

tools.morse-code.metadata.description: Translate text to Morse code and Morse code back to text instantly. Free, private and runs entirely in your browser.
tools.morse-code.faqs.0.question: What is Morse code?
tools.morse-code.faqs.0.answer: Morse code is a method of encoding text as sequences of dots (.) and dashes (-). Each letter and digit has a unique pattern, and words are separated by a slash (/).
tools.morse-code.faqs.1.question: How do I convert text to Morse code?
tools.morse-code.faqs.1.answer: Type or paste your text in the input box. The Morse output updates instantly — letters are separated by spaces and words by slashes.
tools.morse-code.faqs.2.question: How do I convert Morse code back to text?
tools.morse-code.faqs.2.answer: Switch to the “Decode” mode and paste the Morse code using dots, dashes and spaces (words separated by “/”). The decoded text appears instantly.
tools.morse-code.faqs.3.question: What is the SOS signal?
tools.morse-code.faqs.3.answer: SOS is one of the best-known Morse signals: ... --- ... (three dots, three dashes, three dots). It is used as a distress signal.
tools.morse-code.faqs.4.question: Is this tool free?
tools.morse-code.faqs.4.answer: Yes, completely free. All conversion happens in your browser — nothing is uploaded.

tools.px-to-rem.metadata.title: PX to REM Converter
tools.px-to-rem.metadata.description: Convert pixels (px) to rem and rem to pixels with a custom base font size. Free CSS unit converter.
tools.px-to-rem.faqs.0.question: What is rem?
tools.px-to-rem.faqs.0.answer: rem is a CSS unit relative to the root element’s font size (usually html). Unlike em, it isn’t affected by parent font sizes.
tools.px-to-rem.faqs.1.question: What is the base font size?
tools.px-to-rem.faqs.1.answer: The default base is 16px — the browser default — and you can switch to 14, 15, 17, 18 or 20px.
tools.px-to-rem.faqs.2.question: How do I convert px to rem?
tools.px-to-rem.faqs.2.answer: Divide the pixel value by the base font size: 16px ÷ 16 = 1rem. The tool does this instantly.
tools.px-to-rem.faqs.3.question: Why use rem instead of px?
tools.px-to-rem.faqs.3.answer: rem scales with the root font size, which makes responsive layouts easier and respects the user’s browser font-size setting.

tools.password-strength.faqs.0.answer: The score combines length and character variety: uppercase, lowercase, digits and symbols each add points.
tools.password-strength.faqs.1.question: What makes a strong password?
tools.password-strength.faqs.1.answer: At least 12 characters, a mix of upper/lowercase letters, digits and symbols, and no common words or personal info.
tools.password-strength.faqs.2.question: Is my password sent anywhere?
tools.password-strength.faqs.2.answer: No. Everything runs in your browser — your password never leaves your device.
tools.password-strength.faqs.3.question: What is a good score?
tools.password-strength.faqs.3.answer: Aim for “Good” or “Strong”. If you see “Weak” or “Fair”, make the password longer and add more character types.
tools.password-strength.labels.privacy: Your password is analyzed locally in your browser and never sent anywhere.
